title: The Things We Keep
shortLine: A son tries to preserve the person he cannot bear to lose.
synopsis: After his father Jacob dies, George watches his mother Lily’s health fail and devotes himself to the promise of preservation. What begins as love becomes an attempt to bargain with time itself, until the machinery built to defeat loss creates a more terrible kind of absence.
imageAlt: A cool-lit laboratory with glass and scientific equipment
detailLine: Love can become another name for refusing to let go.
underneath: The horror grows from a recognisable impulse: if love is real, surely it should be able to keep someone here. The story examines the moment devotion begins to confuse a person with the fear of losing them.
visualMotifs: A hand separated by a pane
coreQuestion: When does the wish to preserve someone stop serving the person you love and start serving your own grief?

detailImage.alt: Blue-white fractures of ice across a frozen surface
detailImage.caption: Cold can preserve an object without preserving the life inside it.

readerImages.alt: An empty hospital bed in a dimly lit room
readerImages.caption: Before preservation became an obsession, there was a room in which Lily could only be lost.

readerImages.alt: Cold mountain peaks beneath a deep blue night sky
readerImages.caption: A cold beauty that cannot bring anyone back.
